text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Tuesday.

LONDON - A set of disappointing results from bank Barclays Plc and growing concerns about the strength of the pound kept a lid on British stocks Tuesday, dealers and strategists said. With no decisive lead from Wall Street, the leading FTSE 100 index of shares ended 5.5 points lower at 4,332.3.

FRANKFURT - The German DAX index ended market trade Tuesday at yet another all-time closing high, with the main inspiration behind record gains coming from the dollar's ongoing resilience. The DAX index ended up 43.59 points at 3,276.16. In after-market trade, the index stood at 3,230.83, down 29.47.

PARIS - French stocks gave up their early gains Tuesday and closed lower after the dollar slipped from its highs, spurring profit taking in the French market. "The dollar slipped back abruptly, falling below 1.70 German marks," said a dealer. Other traders said the market was ripe for profit-taking after hitting all-time highs in early trading. "Some people may also be a bit nervous ahead of the U.S. CPI (Consumer Price Index) due out tomorrow," another dealer said. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 16.96 points, or 0.64 percent, at 2,617.52 .

ZURICH - Swiss stocks were hit by profit taking late in the session, ending near the day's lows, after reaching an all-time high of 4,548.1 SMI points in early trade. The broad Swiss Performance Index ended off 12.21 points at 2,853.98.

TOKYO - The Tokyo stock market's key index saw its five-day rally end Tuesday as global blue chips lost their shine with investors after recent heavy gains. The Nikkei 225 average fell 279.90 points, or 1.49 percent, to close at 18,470.75.

HONG KONG - Concerns about the health of China's paramount leader, Deng Xiaoping, sent Hong Kong stocks tumbling Tuesday, but the blue-chip Hang Seng Index managed to crawl back from its lows to finish only modestly weaker. The index closed at 13,102.94, off 41.68 points or 0.32 percent.

SYDNEY - A booming bank sector lifted an otherwise lackluster Australian stock market to a record close Tuesday, the market crawling ahead despite a lack of inspiration from offshore markets. The All Ordinaries index climbed 8.5 points to close at 2,501.7.

JOHANNESBURG - South African stocks rose on all fronts Tuesday, with gold stocks climbing 29.9 points, or 2.11 percent, to 1,448.6 points. Industrial stocks rose 52.2 points, or .63 percent, to 8,368.1. The overall index added 51.7 points, a .73 percent increase, closing at 7,094.2.
